messages:
alex: customer reports intermittent 403s on /v1/embeddings after a billing spike. They gave a request_id and asked us to find server logs and repro steps. request_id=0a1b2c3d timestamp=2026-03-15T14:22:10Z

sara: can you paste the full request_id + the exact curl they used? also which key: service token or user key? :thinking:

alex: full request_id=0a1b2c3d. customer used their service key from prod. they also attached a screenshot of the 403 body: `{"error":"forbidden", "code":403}`

ingrid: i'll grep kibana. note: hosted log retention is 7 days for this account. if the event is older we need to pull from archived S3. running a narrow time window +-2m around 2026-03-15T14:22:10Z. query i use:
```
index: logs-prod-*
message: "request_id=0a1b2c3d" OR json.request_id:"0a1b2c3d"
| sort @timestamp desc
```
this should surface the edge + auth traces.

mike: quick repro curl (use their token placeholder):
```
curl -v 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "X-Request-Id: 0a1b2c3d" 
  -d '{"model":"embed-1","input":"test"}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```
if they hit 403 locally with same token it's a token/iam issue. if not, we look network/proxy differences.

support-bot: debug bundle generation: created s3://support-debug/0a1b2c3d-debug.tar.gz (expires in 48h)

ingrid: found auth-service span at 2026-03-15T14:22:11Z. log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T14:22:11.123Z] auth-service ERROR request_id=0a1b2c3d uid=acct-987 reason=token_revoked policy=service-key-rotation
```
this shows token was revoked right before the call. also see a short retry loop from client causing ~6 rapid calls which would explain billing spike.

alex: customer says they rotated API keys around 14:21 and forgot to update one of their backend services. they had a retry policy with exponential backoff max 5 tries. looks like a race where one component kept hitting the old key.

sara: recommendation: tell customer to rotate keys and restart the backend that used the old key. advise patch to treat 403 as non-retriable for this endpoint to avoid billing loops. can you attach the kibana query + curl for them?

ingrid: attaching both. also note: if logs fall outside retention, run `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs-archive/<date>/support-archive-*.gz - | zgrep \"request_id=0a1b2c3d\"` to search archived bundles.

mike: assigned infra/alerts to check whether token-revocation events should auto-trigger a customer-facing email. opening INC-4321.

alex: i'll send the customer a concise repro plan: 1) confirm key rotation, 2) run the curl above with their current token, 3) check for 403 and share X-Request-Id header (we have 0a1b2c3d), 4) share debug bundle link if issue persists. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sara: closing loop: customer confirmed restart and error resolved. followup: i recommended limiting retries on 403 and we suggested a short postmortem with the customer on billing exposure.

mike: quick note for ops: consider alerting on >3 token_revoked events for same account within 5m — that pattern maps to accidental rotations.

alex: thanks team, forwarding repro steps and kibana snippet to acct team.
